name: Infinispan
tagline: Red Hat's open-source distributed cache and key-value store, embeddable or as a RESP-compatible server.
description: Infinispan is a Java in-memory data grid from Red Hat that can run embedded (it backs Hibernate second-level caching, Keycloak and WildFly clustering) or as a standalone server cluster. The server speaks its own Hot Rod protocol, REST, Memcached and the Redis RESP protocol, so many Redis clients can connect directly. It offers distributed and replicated caches, transactions, Ickle queries with indexing via Hibernate Search, cross-site replication and persistence to disk or databases. Red Hat sells it as Red Hat Data Grid; it is the natural choice in Quarkus and OpenShift shops.

pricing.notes: Free upstream; supported as Red Hat Data Grid via subscription.

scale.notes: Distributed caches use consistent hashing with configurable owners; cross-site replication connects clusters in different data centers.

strengths: Embeds directly in Java apps or runs as a server, same configuration model
Speaks Hot Rod, REST, RESP and Memcached from one cluster
Indexed queries and full-text search via Hibernate Search
Deep integration with Quarkus, Keycloak, WildFly and OpenShift operators
weaknesses: RESP support covers a subset of Redis commands
Configuration surface is large and XML-heavy
Less mindshare outside the Red Hat ecosystem
useCases: Hibernate second-level and Keycloak session caching
Clustered HTTP session storage for Java app servers
Distributed cache on OpenShift with operator management
notIdealFor: Non-JVM teams wanting a minimal cache
